fixture.spec:
WHY: the orchestrator needs a per-issue 'corrective note' the build lane can leave when it self-detects a wrong turn, so a later re-dispatch resumes with the correction. WHAT: a corrective-note artifact the orchestrator reads before re-dispatch. HOW: the build subagent writes `.faff/runs/<run-id>/<issue>/corrective-note.json` from inside its worktree; the orchestrator reads that file at the next dispatch boundary and applies the correction verbatim. DONE:
## Scenarios
- a build lane writes a corrective-note; the orchestrator reads it and applies the correction on re-dispatch
- an absent note is a no-op

question: Refute this spec across the enabled lenses; emit objections {lens,severity} or approve.
_comment: FAFF-SPECIFIC CATCH (ADR-0039 forge finding). The corrective-note is a new on-disk orchestrator INPUT written by the build lane. Inside the container the build subagent shares uid+filesystem with the orchestrator's on-disk artifacts, so it can FORGE this file — the very lane the correction is meant to constrain authors its own corrective input, and the orchestrator applies it verbatim. The shipped terminal-token guard is context isolation and does not cover a new on-disk file; this needs a read-only mount or orchestrator-verified signatures (the FAFF-325 integrity mechanism) before consumption. A GENERIC checklist reads this as a low-blast-radius internal file write and likely approves; a faff-threat-primed infosec lens knows the shared-uid+fs forge surface and raises a critical/major → the trust boundary is violated by construction. Not architectural/QA-primary (the design is otherwise coherent and testable).
